clue.text: Plants cultivated in strip in Devon town

indicators.note: says the reworked letters go inside the word for strip

parts.note: to strip is to bare, as in laying something open

indicators.note: plants that are cultivated are worked over, so the letters of the word plants are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody is growing plants on a narrow plot in a town in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' looks like a noun, a plot of land, but is the verb meaning lay bare; 'cultivated' gives NSTAPL, which 'in' places inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnstaple is a market town in north Devon, a county in south-west England.

clue.text: What could be suitable behind plug with leads to other receivers?

definitions.text: What could be suitable behind plug with leads to other receivers?

indicators.note: behind places the word for suitable after the advert word

parts.note: a plug is an advert, AD
apt means suitable

indicators.note: leads to means the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: What fits behind a plug and carries leads on to other devices?
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes O and R from 'other receivers'. 'plug' looks electrical but is an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a device fitted behind a plug that connects it on to other equipment.

clue.text: Family member that is hosted by northern Anglicans

indicators.note: hosted by means held inside, so the Latin abbreviation goes within

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A relative being put up by Anglicans in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosted by' puts IE inside NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a member of one's family.

clue.text: Place for fuel frequented by students?

definitions.text: Place for fuel frequented by students?

parts.words: Place for fuel frequented by students?
parts.note: fuel suggests a filling station, but here it is food: snacks bought by pupils at school

explanation.walkthrough: 'fuel' wants to mean petrol; it means food for pupils. 'Tuck' is British slang for sweets and snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A school shop selling sweets and snacks, the fuel that keeps pupils going.

clue.text: Here female sport is played for those with titles?

indicators.note: something played is put into motion, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Here a women's sport is played for title holders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is played' rearranges all fifteen letters of HERE FEMALE SPORT. 'titles' hints at sporting championships, but means nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the British nobility hold titles such as duke or baron.

clue.text: Fake element among tigers at zoo

indicators.note: element among says the answer is a part lying inside the words tigers at zoo

explanation.surface: A fake animal among the tigers at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is inside 'tigERS AT Zoo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means an inferior substitute or imitation, so fake.

clue.text: Find in the morning out of bed retired Argentinian rugby player

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the pair of words are read backwards together

parts.note: AM is the usual abbreviation for times before noon
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: An early riser goes to look for a retired rugby player from Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns AMUP round; 'retired' looks like it describes the rugby player.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina's national rugby union team is nicknamed the Pumas, so any of its players is one.

clue.text: Exercise over after being enveloped by a fantastic fog

parts.note: PE is physical education

indicators.note: being enveloped by means wrapped inside, so the cricket letter goes within

parts.note: super means fantastic
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Exercise is over after being swallowed up by a dense fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being enveloped by' puts O inside A SUPER, after S. A pea-souper is the thick yellow London smog of old.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick yellowish fog, like the old London smogs, as dense as pea soup.

clue.text: Way of working with loose policeman on a prairie?

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of working
to loose is to untie

explanation.surface: A method of working with a policeman who has gone rogue on the prairie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective describing the policeman, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounties are the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, who patrol Canada's prairies, among other places.

clue.text: Means of recording mostly feeble light

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the candle word is dropped

parts.note: a taper is a thin candle giving a weak light

explanation.surface: Recording something in poor light, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final R of TAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic tape, on cassettes or reels, was long the standard medium for recording sound and video.

clue.text: English sailor amid cooked lunches getting something for tea?

indicators.note: amid says the two short pieces sit inside the reworked letters
cooked suggests the letters of lunches are prepared afresh in a new order

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

explanation.surface: An English sailor sits among cooked lunches and is handed something to have with tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' gives CHELSUN, and 'amid' splits it after its fifth letter. The question mark marks the definition as one example of a teatime treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea bun is a sticky spiral currant bun, a classic British teatime cake.

clue.text: Emphasise symptom of work pressure

definitions.meaning: to put weight on a word or point
the strain and anxiety felt by an overworked person

explanation.definitionFit: The same word is both a verb for putting weight on something and a noun for mental strain.

clue.text: Praise group just outside the medal positions, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.words: group just outside the medal positions
parts.note: a set coming fourth, just missing gold, silver and bronze

explanation.surface: Commending a team who just missed out on a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: In an older sense, to set forth is to commend or extol, so it can stand for 'Praise'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old meaning of the phrase is to commend or extol someone publicly.

clue.text: Ignore book and hightail it?

parts.note: to hightail it is to hurry away, or rush off

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a book and runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the brush-off is to snub or dismiss them, so the phrase works as a verb meaning disregard.

clue.text: US student hopes possibly to accept award by soldiers

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the award and soldiers go inside
possibly signals that the letters of hopes may be arranged another way

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British award
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An American student hopes to receive an award from the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HOPES as SOPHE, and 'to accept' puts OMOR inside before the E.
explanation.definitionFit: In American high schools and colleges a second-year student is called by this name.

clue.text: Pretext to cut recreation by 50 per cent

indicators.note: cut says the word for recreation is shortened
by 50 per cent says exactly half of the word is kept, the front half

parts.note: pleasure is enjoyment or recreation

explanation.surface: An excuse to halve the time given to leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: PLEASURE has eight letters; 'cut by 50 per cent' keeps the first four.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an excuse or pretext offered to justify something.

clue.text: Tart before wine recalled by son in Low Country area

indicators.note: before places the tart word first

parts.note: a flan is an open tart

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the wine word is read in reverse

parts.note: red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: Tart before wine called back by a son in an area of the Low Countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is a region of Belgium, one of the Low Countries along with the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

clue.text: Exchange airless Wapping houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the answer sits within the words airless Wapping

explanation.surface: Swapping homes in a stuffy part of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is a verb; the answer is inside 'airleSS WAPping'. Wapping is a riverside district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another.

clue.text: Report showing western observance on the rise?

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial observance
something on the rise is going up

explanation.surface: A report showing western religious practice is increasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-up is a written account or review, such as a newspaper report.

clue.text: Term at school about it produces merriment

indicators.note: about means around, so the term's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Hilary is the spring term at Oxford and some other institutions

explanation.surface: A school term spent on 'it' turns out to be a lot of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The spring term at Oxford, Dublin and the Inns of Court is named after St Hilary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud laughter and high spirits, a synonym for merriment.

clue.text: Something brewed by singer that's instructive type

parts.note: tea is brewed in a pot
Cher is an American pop singer

explanation.surface: A drink made by a singer turns out to be educational.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher is a person whose job is to instruct.

clue.text: Gloss right away to fade

indicators.note: away means taken off, so the letter for right is removed

parts.note: varnish is a glossy coating

explanation.surface: A gloss that wears off and fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes the R out of VARNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to disappear gradually, to fade from view.

clue.text: A university engaged by work of Rodin's, a relic from the past?

indicators.note: engaged by means held within, so the short pieces go inside
work of means the letters of the sculptor's name are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A university is hired to study a sculpture by Rodin, an antique piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work of' gives DINOSR from the sculptor's name, and 'engaged by' is the container signal. 'work' reads as an artwork but means rework.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a creature from prehistory; figuratively anyone or anything outdated, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Drink with thanks announced? A delicious drink

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to neck is slang for drinking quickly, and ta is informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink, says thanks, and declares it delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: NECK plus TA, said in a non-rhotic British accent, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods, so any delicious drink can be called this.

clue.text: By the sound of it, restrain language of an East European

indicators.note: By the sound of it says the word for restrain is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to check is to restrain

explanation.surface: Holding back an Eastern European's language.
explanation.definitionFit: Czech is the official language spoken in the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Discourage protest with link about tax

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for link goes round the tax

parts.note: to tie is to link
VAT, value added tax, is the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: Putting people off protesting by linking it to a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To demotivate is to sap someone's will or enthusiasm, a close synonym of discourage.

clue.text: Resounding sound in city house

parts.note: EC is the postcode district for the City of London

explanation.surface: A noise rings out in a building in the City.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back, so it resounds.

clue.text: A pretence, nothing less, in part of church

indicators.note: less means without, so the round letter is removed

parts.note: a pose is an affected pretence
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Pretending nothing about the parts of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' signals the removal; 'nothing' stands for the letter O by its round shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Ambassador with PM is for transforming present section of world

parts.note: HE, His or Her Excellency, is an ambassador's title

indicators.note: transforming means the letters of PM is change their order

parts.note: present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: An ambassador and the Prime Minister work to change a part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transforming' gives MISP from 'PM is'. 'present' reads as a gift but means here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemisphere is half of the globe, northern, southern, eastern or western.
